findings.summary: There is no design waiting to approve anywhere in the product, and no deck card type for design approval was ever shown. The only related item is a board task 'Review and approve landing page design' (assigned to me, Blocked) with no design visible on it, so a user cannot approve a design from the Deck or see what they are approving.

The spot-check card shows the judge's reasoning and the verdict, but not the criterion being judged ('CTA button is above the fold on mobile' — visible only after opening the run page). A user must open the run to know what the verdict was about.

In Deck (card) view, a single click on an answer option does nothing and gives no visible selected state — the answer only registers after click + Enter. The same option answers instantly with one click in List view. Twice I concluded the buttons were broken before discovering the two-step flow.

Undo on a stale-brief acknowledgment reports a successful click on the toast's Undo button, but the stale-brief card never returns to the queue — after reload the deck showed only a regenerated decision, not the stale-brief card. Undo works for decisions but silently fails for stale-brief acknowledgments.

The stale-brief card offers only one resolution — 'Acknowledge — the change is cosmetic' — even when the brief edit added a substantive functional requirement (a new above-the-fold CTA constraint). There is no path from the card to recompile or propagate the change.
Background polling errors accumulate in the console: /api/dashboard returns HTTP 405 roughly every 30 seconds, and /api/projects/{id}/brief returns 404 for projects without briefs.

Batch controls exist in List view (Select all pending, an 'Answer all selected with…' box, batch Dismiss and Defer 7d) and successfully batch-answered a selection, but the queue never held more than 2 items in this environment so a ten-plus batch could not be observed.

At session start the Deck held only a decision and a verdict spot-check. The design-to-approve and the pre-flagged stale brief promised by the scenario were absent; the stale-brief card only appeared after I edited a brief myself, and the same decision regenerates every few minutes after being answered.
